q: The alcohols may be considered as ____ of alkanes.
e: The alcohols may be considered as derivatives of alkanes. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: The replacement of one hydrogen atom in an alkane by a ____ (-OH) group gives the corresponding alcohol.
e: The replacement of one hydrogen atom in an alkane by a hydroxyl (-OH) group gives the corresponding alcohol. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: They form a homologous series with the general formula ____ (or) $C_nH_{2n+2}O$ where n is a number equal to or greater than 1.
e: They form a homologous series with the general formula C_nH2n+1OH (or) C_nH2n+2O where n is a number equal to or greater than 1. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once. In a homologous-series formula, n is the number of carbon atoms in that member.

q: The common name of an alcohol combines the name of the ____ group with the word alcohol.

q: Alcohols are given their respective names by adding ____ instead of -ane of alkane.

q: Alcohols form ____ isomerism due to the different structures of C-skeleton in the longer chain.

e: The basic carbon skeleton remains unchanged in the isomers, but a hydroxyl group (-OH) can be located in different positions, so they are positional isomers. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: Ethene and steam are passed over a ____ catalyst at 570 °C and 60~70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol.
